ambiguities: Duplicate game ids: dedupe applied after filtering invalid games (first valid occurrence in sorted file order, CFB before CFB26); a first invalid file would not shadow a later valid one.
File order for 'first' = CFB then CFB26, each sorted by filename.
Integer parsing uses Python int() on stripped strings; non-integer text (e.g. '7.0') makes the game invalid.
Touchdown entries lacking team/scoringType: no scoringType name match -> not a touchdown; touchdown with unparseable team id counted as belonging to neither side (can make first_td missing).
Pool for a date = all games earlier in sorted order than the first game of that date (strictly earlier date) with season >= S-1.
Teams absent from a pool fit have coefficients 0 (equivalent to including them with ridge penalty); ep for such teams = b0 + 0 terms.
Games whose ridge value is missing: kernel x missing -> row excluded as reference and gets missing output.
qj_hi 'smallest index attaining max' uses exact integer equality of c_k.
pst ratio computed as ratio of kernel sums (kernel denominators cancel); missing when E[total]==0.
tdc_var uses kernel with td missingness mask shared by E[td] and E[td^2] (same reference rows).
Kernel MIN_REF count applied per event after masks on the reference rows; ratio columns (pst) use unmasked c so same count as qj_hi.
completionAttempts split on '/' or '-', second number; rushingAttempts and totalYards parsed via int() of displayValue (commas not handled).
Box team entries mapped to home/away by team id; missing id for either side -> yards/plays/rush missing.
Date: co.date parsed as UTC minus 10 hours then calendar date.
2D kernel (rtc_tie) uses |x_mar| for both reference and query rows.
Drives rule was clarified after the first comparison: drives.previous entries with no (or unparseable) team id are ignored, counting for neither side and not making counts missing.
Missing ridge target in pool games: ranks still counted over whole pool, per brief.
